Its steady average from elapsed `220-490s` was about `403/sec`, its late pre-stop band about `408/sec`, and drain about `372/sec`; it crossed `10,000,000` at elapsed `442s` with `0` parser errors, retries, duplicates, or terminal markers. This established PVE34 as the best practical Nyx profile for that data band and showed that the DB/write path—not fetch—was limiting despite idle headroom. It also followed a hard-kill recovery in which the next normal parser start found `1,336` gap ranges / `1,376` missing IDs from DB truth and repaired them without manual gap repair.

The later durable autonomy summary, created and updated `2026-05-25 08:55 PDT`, superseded treating PVE34 or any worker count as the parser's identity. answer.answer: Prioritize the `/in/playerActivity` cache-miss path outside profile work. Replace request-time rebuilds with stale-while-revalidate: serve a longer-lived stale value, refresh in the background under a lock, and prevent web requests from paying for Redis shard scans. Separately, change `/p/:identifier/raids` so fast local raid statistics render first; defer collectible/progress enrichment and load Pantheon only when selected, or share/cache its Bungie collectibles fetch.

claims.value: The highest-value non-profile target is `GET /in/playerActivity`, ranked first in the saved optimization candidates. Over 7 days it had 13,210 RUM calls (avg 3.69 s, p75 1.09 s, p95 12.03 s) and 23,255 APM spans (avg 1.99 s, p75 2 ms, p95 13.03 s). The 2 ms p75 combined with the roughly 13 s p95 identifies a severe cache-miss tail on a high-volume resource used by analytics home.

Implement stale-while-revalidate for `/in/playerActivity`: retain a longer-lived stale cache value, serve it immediately, and perform refreshes in the background under a distributed lock so only one rebuild runs. The code-path reason is that `apiPlayerActivity` reads the `apiPlayerActivity` cache but falls back to synchronous `memcache.GetPlayerActivity`; meanwhile `sweeperbot.cachePlayerActivity` refreshes every 5 minutes using a matching 5 minute TTL, creating an expiry race in which foreground requests perform the Redis scan. The saved 24-hour logs recorded 68 foreground rebuilds and 204 shard logs, with shard-scan p95 about 18 s and math p95 about 16 s. Preserve the Discord-style missing-cache behavior—no data instead of rebuilding in the command path—as the failure fallback.

On `/p/:identifier/raids`, the bottleneck is Bungie collectibles enrichment, not raid SQL or images. `loadLogbookRaidSources` waits for every concurrent source, including slow `bungie.GetD2ProfileStats(..., bungie.ProfileWCollectibles)`, before responding; `LogbookRaidsPage` then holds the real page behind `RaidsLoading`. Pantheon also starts immediately and repeats a separate `ProfileWCollectibles` request before its tab is opened. Change the route to return and render the shell plus fast local clears/full clears/carries/fastest data first, defer collectible/progress enrichment, and lazy-load Pantheon when selected or share/cache the Bungie result server-side. The evidence baseline is raid RUM p95 4.00 s and APM p95 3.77 s, while local `raiddifficultysummaries`, `raidcarries`, and `raidseals` sources were only about 2.7 ms, 10.1 ms, and 0.6 ms at the reported 95th percentile; images had p95 264 ms and are secondary.

After the `/in/playerActivity` change, measure exact-route APM count/avg/p75/p95, RUM resource count/avg/p75/p95, foreground-rebuild count, shard-log count and shard-scan/math p95, plus stale age, refresh success/failure, lock contention, and concurrent rebuild count. Compare against the saved baselines of APM p75 2 ms/p95 13.03 s, RUM p95 12.03 s, 68 foreground rebuilds, shard-scan p95 about 18 s, and math p95 about 16 s; verify foreground rebuilds and duplicate rebuilds approach zero without unacceptable data staleness. After the raid-route change, separately measure time to shell, time to first local raid scaffold/cards, raid and Pantheon request timing/count, exact-route RUM/APM p75/p95, Bungie `ProfileWCollectibles` call count/latency, and whether Pantheon is absent until tab selection. Compare against raid RUM p95 4.00 s and APM p95 3.77 s, and confirm local raid content renders without waiting for collectibles while enrichment still completes correctly.

answer.answer: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer. It preserves learned knowledge together with resumable work state, treating Obsidian as a prototype corpus and human projection rather than the product boundary. The completed retrieval benchmark remains useful as a regression baseline, but the expanded evaluation must demonstrate successful continuation and advancement of real work—including computation, verification, iteration, and correct durable handoffs.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable agent context and durable-work layer and protocol. Its category is durable machine continuity for agents across research, planning, implementation, operations, verification, and handoff—not primarily a notes app, wiki, transcript archive, synchronized folder, retrieval system/product, or memory database.

Beyond learned durable knowledge, Straylight must preserve the live state needed to resume and advance work: goals, evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, artifacts, computations, unresolved/open questions, rejected paths or approaches, checkpoints, current state, and resumable next actions. A later agent must be able to inspect how that state was reached, reopen and query it, compute over and verify it, revise it as evidence changes, checkpoint it, hand it off, and leave a better durable state behind. Task-scoped resumable checkpoints are independent of durable semantic-memory promotion.

Obsidian is not the product boundary because Straylight is agent-first, while Obsidian and Markdown are prototype corpora, human-readable projections, and export formats rather than the canonical interaction or storage representation. Metis organizes the human knowledge base and supplies the first representative corpus; Straylight is the portable agent context and durable-work product designed over that kind of corpus. Full source artifacts and evidence remain authoritative and inspectable, while notes, summaries, embeddings, indexes, and context packs are representations or derived aids rather than truth boundaries.

The first benchmark was too narrow because it evaluated retrieval readiness rather than the full durable-work product: 20 frozen questions and 53 gold evidence items compared direct full-file access, one-shot BM25 top-k, and a minimal deterministic Memory Workspace exercising `memory.open`, `memory.query`, and `memory.read`; model-directed `memory.compute` and `memory.verify` remained untested. Policy 0.2 and one-shot top-k each passed 17 of 20 cases, but top-k recovered 48 of 53 evidence items versus the workspace’s 46 of 53 and used about 1,070 mean estimated tokens versus 2,932, so the workspace hypothesis was not demonstrated; policy 0.2 is therefore only a frozen regression baseline, and its tuned score is not holdout evidence. The expanded primary evaluation must prove that a fresh agent can successfully resume and advance real work—iterate after changing constraints, compute, inspect complete sources and artifacts, reason about time, supersession and contradictions, verify before acting, continue incidents, and leave correct durable next-state and handoff artifacts. It must compare direct filesystem tools, an agent-first workspace with model-directed `open`, `query`, `read`, `compute`, `verify`, checkpoint and revision behavior, and fixed handoff/context packs, using untouched blinded cases across required Warmind/Charlemagne performance and incident work, StarRupture factory planning, Switzerland trip planning, and Straylight’s own evolution. Correctness, completeness, evidence-chain recall, citation/source accuracy, temporal and supersession handling, source fidelity, reasoning quality, recovery from poor initial retrieval, and durable-state quality must outrank latency and cost; the required improvement threshold and sufficiently large, varied untouched holdout set remain unresolved, and no canonical storage-engine decision is allowed before this blinded model-answer gate.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable agent context and durable-work layer for agents. It is agent-first infrastructure for durable machine continuity across research, planning, implementation, operations, verification, and handoff—not primarily a notes app, wiki, synchronized folder, transcript archive, retrieval product, or memory database.

Beyond learned memory, Straylight must preserve the live state of work: evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, artifacts, computations, unresolved questions, rejected paths, checkpoints, and the next safe action. A later agent must be able to resume the work, inspect how the state was reached, revise it as evidence changes, verify it, and leave a better durable state behind.

Obsidian and human-readable notes are useful projections and prototype inputs, while the vault is an excellent representative prototype and evaluation corpus. They are not the product boundary or canonical interaction model, and raw Markdown is not assumed to be Straylight’s only or canonical storage representation; Straylight is the portable agent context and durable-work product built over such corpora.

Reasoning quality, source fidelity, durable-state quality, and ability to iterate must outrank retrieval recall, storage convenience, or deployment convenience.
